title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that compares a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a deterministic 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; only downstream deterministic validation and the guarded arm's single permitted repair call could create paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total hosted model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret these artifact‑grounded results in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator coverage, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises operational efficiency but raises safety concerns: incorrect ordering, transient invariant violations, protected‑field interference, and other multi‑step sequencing errors can convert plausible command lists into harmful actions. Recent surveys and domain studies document frequent LLM hallucinations and structured‑output fragility that degrade correctness for code and configuration outputs, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate, to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so any paired difference is attributable to deterministic validation decisions and the permitted repair call rather than to first‑pass generation differences (prompting, constrained decoding, or sampling variance).

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministically selected tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus and archived deterministic validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing completed_pairs = 1000, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, repair calls = 5, and model configuration metadata. (3) Transparent reporting of the preregistered confirmatory result (exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625), preregistered descriptive bootstrap summaries (95% CI = [0.001,0.01], seed = 1729), and artifact‑grounded discussion of interpretive limits imposed by shared_initial_candidate semantics and near‑unity baseline validity.
sections.related_work:
Existing literature documents two adjacent findings motivating this study. First, LLMs produce structured‑output errors, hallucinations, and strong prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness for code and configuration tasks [1],[2]. Second, systems and benchmark research propose and demonstrate architectures that pair generation with deterministic validation, constrained decoding, or iterative repair (generate→validate→repair) and argue these pipelines reduce unsafe or non‑executable outputs in structured domains and prototypes for NetOps [3],[4],[5].

Prior NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, governance, proof‑carrying proposals and digital‑twin validation for safer execution; these works present prototypes and architectural arguments showing that operational reliability depends on validator fidelity, orchestration protocols, and governance layers rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6]. Our study complements these contributions by providing a preregistered, paired estimand that isolates how much value deterministic downstream validation and a single permitted repair add when the generator output is held constant across conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, frozen design, and estimand. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen before any hosted model calls (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and prespecified sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under the archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Hence, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). The design therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained‑decoding arms that were not executed.

Modeling and validator configuration. The declared execution model is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and the orchestration adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), a digital‑twin emulator that enforces manifest workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and specified missingness treatments; all seeds and task selection rules were fixed prior to execution.

Task corpus and scoring. Tasks were drawn deterministically from challenging_workflow_stress_v1 by the preregistered ordinal selection rule producing exactly 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The validator compares parsed candidate command sequences against these manifest constraints; scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary validity outcome used in the paired analysis.

Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The preregistered adapter audited provider calls and caching. Execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 2000, completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. The analysis executor applied the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment; sensitivity analyses were preregistered but unneeded because failed episodes = 0.
sections.results:
Execution and raw accounting. The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 (cache_miss_count = 1005) with shared_initial_generation = 1000 and repair = 5; cross‑condition cache reuse was not observed and all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary summaries and exploratory notes. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. A directional one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory inference. Representative artifacts and validator traces (archived per episode) show five validator‑triggered repair sequences where the single allowed repair call produced an accepted candidate upon revalidation. Total hosted model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5).

Inferential hierarchy and bootstrap sensitivity (concise statement). The exact two‑sided McNemar is the preregistered confirmatory analysis and it did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI and the one‑sided McNemar are reported only as preregistered descriptive and exploratory summaries respectively; they do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory outcome. The bootstrap CI can exclude zero under extreme cases of very sparse discordant counts because resampling from a dataset with n10=5 and n01=0 produces nonzero percentile bounds; this sensitivity is artifact‑grounded and reproducible using the archived contingency table and bootstrap_seed = 1729.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory outcome and interpretive limits. The preregistered primary test (exact two‑sided McNemar, p = 0.0625) is the confirmatory inference and is not significant at two‑sided α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001,0.01]) was preregistered as a descriptive summary and is sensitive to the extreme sparsity of discordant pairs; we therefore treat the bootstrap interval as an informative but nonconfirmatory descriptor. The one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) is explicitly labeled post‑hoc/exploratory because the preregistration did not specify a one‑sided direction.

Mechanistic consequences under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms reused the same sampled initial candidate, any observed improvement must arise from deterministic validation decisions and the permitted repair(s). The five observed repairs illustrate that a validator with sufficient rule coverage can correct ordering/sequence violations in some episodes. However, the low repair count constrains inference about repair efficacy across diverse failure modes: the guarded pipeline can only benefit when the validator detects a defect that the single allowed repair call can remediate. Distinguishing whether low repair counts stem from generator correctness, corpus characteristics, or validator permissiveness requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity and external generalization. Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5's rule coverage; omitted semantic checks would overstate measured success. Internal validity is strong with deterministic seeding, no failed episodes, and complete pair accounting, but the shared_initial_candidate design precludes measuring benefits from improved first‑pass generation (e.g., constrained decoding or prompt redesign). External validity is limited by the synthetic corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini); conclusions do not generalize across models, heterogeneous vendor environments, or production operational complexity without further study.

Operational implications and preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows that downstream verifier‑guided repair can avert particular unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups supported by the archive include: (1) independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding effects; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluate multiple model families with aligned power calculations for plausible baseline failure regimes.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls used = 1005. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

Preregistration identifier: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains under the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
